html:
Nutmeg trees were brought to Grenada in 1843, from the spice islands of the East Indies, and became the island's main crop. Grenada is called the Isle of Spice, and a nutmeg appears on its flag.

After sugar declined, many freed families grew nutmeg and cocoa on small plots. By the 20th century Grenada was one of the world's two big nutmeg producers, with Indonesia, whose Banda Islands were the spice's first home.

The nutmeg growers' cooperative ran the trade. In 2004 Hurricane Ivan flattened most of the trees, which take years to bear fruit, and the trade has only partly recovered.
